recognize_zh: 紅血球背景中一條細長彎曲、深藍色的線狀蟲體，體內充滿核柱，前端外側可見淡藍色鞘膜延伸，尾端逐漸變細；有鞘、體態平滑彎曲的微絲蟲（microfilaria），配合臨床符合班氏絲蟲（Wuchereria bancrofti）。
features: Elongated, gracefully curved thread-like organism many times the length of a red cell diameter
Body filled with a column of deeply basophilic nuclei
Pale blue sheath visibly extending beyond the anterior end
Tapering tail that thins to a fine point, apparently free of nuclei at the tip (resolution-limited)
Dense red cell background typical of a thick area of blood film
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single microfilaria lying among densely packed red cells. The organism is long and smoothly curved, with a column of basophilic nuclei and a pale staining sheath projecting beyond the anterior end, and a tail that tapers to a fine point. Image resolution does not allow reliable assessment of the terminal nuclei or cephalic space. The findings are consistent with a sheathed microfilaria, suggestive of Wuchereria bancrofti in the appropriate clinical setting.

ddx.vs: Brugia microfilariae are also sheathed but show kinks, a pink-staining sheath on Giemsa, and two separate terminal nuclei in the tail, whereas W. bancrofti has a smooth curve with no nuclei at the tail tip.
Loa loa microfilariae are sheathed but have nuclei extending continuously to the tail tip and circulate by day.
Mansonella microfilariae are smaller, unsheathed, and have a blunt tail with nuclei to the tip.
